label: Auto-detect
description: Let Memorium detect the file format automatically
exportSteps: Export your data using any guide below
Upload the file here — Memorium will pick the right parser

label: Facebook / Instagram / Messenger
description: Meta “Download Your Information” export (ZIP or extracted folder)
exportSteps: Log into Facebook or Instagram (must have account access)
Go to Settings → Your activity → Download your information
Or visit facebook.com/dyi directly
Select the profile (Facebook, Instagram, or both)
Choose JSON format (not HTML)
Select date range: All time
Include: Posts, Messages, Photos and videos, and any other categories you want
Create export and wait for Meta’s email (can take up to 48 hours)
Download the ZIP and upload it here
tips: Do this before an account is memorialized or deleted — Instagram has no post-death export
Facebook legacy contacts can download some data after memorialization, but not messages
Messenger threads are included in the same Meta export bundle

label: WhatsApp
description: WhatsApp chat export as a .txt file
exportSteps: Open WhatsApp on your phone
Open the chat you want to save
Tap the contact or group name at the top
Scroll down and tap Export chat
Choose Without media (smaller file) or Include media
Save or share the .txt file to your computer
Upload the .txt file here (one chat per file)
tips: Repeat for each conversation you want in the archive
Media files are not imported in this POC — text messages only
Export while you still have phone access to the account

label: Android SMS / SMS Backup & Restore
description: XML backup from the SMS Backup & Restore app (Android)
exportSteps: Install SMS Backup & Restore from the Google Play Store on the Android phone
Open the app and tap Backup
Choose SMS (and optionally MMS)
Select a local folder or cloud destination for the backup file
Wait for the backup to complete — file will be named sms-*.xml
Transfer the .xml file to your computer (USB, email, Google Drive, etc.)
Upload the .xml file here
tips: Works with most Android phones and carriers
For Google Messages specifically, you can also use Google Takeout (see Google Messages guide)
Back up before resetting or replacing the phone

label: Google Messages
description: Google Takeout export or Messages JSON backup
exportSteps: Sign in at takeout.google.com with the Google account linked to Messages
Click Deselect all, then check only Messages (and any related items)
Choose export format: ZIP, split if large
Choose delivery method (download link or Drive)
Create export and wait for Google’s email
Download and unzip — look for JSON files inside the Messages folder
Upload the .json file or entire Takeout ZIP here
tips: RCS / Google Messages sync requires the account to be active at export time
If you use Messages on Android without Google backup, use SMS Backup & Restore instead
Takeout exports can be large — allow time for download

label: iPhone iMessage
description: chat.db from an iPhone backup, or CSV from export tools
exportSteps: Option A — chat.db (full archive):
1. Create an encrypted iPhone backup on Mac (Finder) or Windows (iTunes)
2. Use iMazing, iBackup Viewer, or iPhone Backup Extractor to locate chat.db
3. chat.db path: Backup → HomeDomain → Library → SMS → chat.db
4. Copy chat.db to your computer and upload it here
Option B — CSV (simpler):
1. Open iMazing or iBackup Viewer
2. Select Messages → choose a conversation or export all
3. Export as CSV with columns: Date, Sender, Text
4. Upload the .csv file here
tips: Apple does not offer a built-in iMessage export — you must use a backup or third-party tool
Export while you have the phone or an existing backup — memorialized accounts cannot be accessed
chat.db requires an unencrypted backup on Mac, or tools that can read encrypted backups

label: Email (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail)
description: Gmail Takeout .mbox archive or individual .eml files
exportSteps: Gmail: go to takeout.google.com → select Mail → export as .mbox
Outlook: File → Open & Export → Import/Export → export to .pst, then convert to .eml/.mbox with a converter, or save individual messages as .eml
Apple Mail: select messages → File → Save As → Raw Message Source (.eml)
Thunderbird: install ImportExportTools NG addon → export folder as .eml or mbox
Upload the .mbox file, a folder of .eml files (zip first), or individual .eml files here
tips: For a loved one’s account, export while you still have login access or legacy access
Gmail .mbox from Takeout is the most reliable format for bulk import
Zip a folder of .eml files before uploading via the web UI

label: Photos & Videos
description: Folder of photos and videos from any source
exportSteps: Collect photos and videos into a single folder on your computer
Sources: camera roll export, Google Photos Takeout, iCloud download, USB copy from phone
Google Photos: takeout.google.com → select Google Photos → download and unzip
iCloud: icloud.com/photos → select → download, or use the iCloud for Windows/Mac app
Zip the folder if uploading via web UI, or use CLI: npm run cli -- import ./path/to/photos
tips: Memorium uses file dates for timeline ordering — EXIF extraction coming in a future update
For Google Photos Takeout, import the media folder after unzipping
